parole.significato: Used to form the names of cities and towns, especially in Persian- and Urdu-speaking areas.
parole.testo: From Urdu آباد (-ābād) and Persian ـآباد (-âbâd).

parole.significato: A sister that is older than oneself; also used as a term of familiarity or respect toward a woman that is older.
parole.testo: From Urdu آپا (āpā) / Bengali আপা (apa).

parole.significato: A form of textile block-printing found primarily in Sindh, Pakistan.
parole.testo: Likely from Urdu اجرک (ajrak).

parole.significato: older sister
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu باجی (bājī), from Classical Persian باجی (bāji), from Ottoman Turkish باجی (bacı), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *bāča.

parole.significato: A large iron pan having two handles, especially used in Pakistani cuisine
parole.testo: From Urdu بالٹی (baalti, “pail”), originally coined by Birmingham restaurateur Afzal Butt because English people had difficulty pronouncing karahi, the name of the dish used for cooking this food.

parole.significato: Belonging to a certain revivalist movement within Sunni Islam.
parole.testo: From Urdu بریلوی (barelvī); which means "of Bareilly" from Bareilly, a city in Uttar Pradesh, India; the location in which the movement began.

parole.significato: Salawat; The uttering of specific phrases to compliment the prophet Muhammad and his family whenever he is mentioned or…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu دُرُود (durūd), from Classical Persian دُرُود (durūd).

parole.significato: A source of great wealth, especially a mine.
parole.testo: From Urdu گولْکُنْڈَہ (golkunḍa), itself from Telugu గొల్లకొండ (gollakoṇḍa), from గొల్ల (golla, “of or pertaining to shepherds”) + కొండ (koṇḍa, “hill”).

parole.significato: A wedlease (temporary marriage) to a stranger undertaken prior to remarriage to an ex, that is to make the remarriage h…
parole.testo: From Urdu حلالہ (halāla), the practice being called in Eastern Persian حلاله (halâla), while Iranian Persian uses محلل (mohallal), the Arabic term being تَحْلِيل (taḥlīl), scilicet نِكَاح التَحْلِيل (nikāḥ at-taḥlīl), زَوَاج التَحْلِيل (zawāj at-taḥlīl).

parole.significato: In South Asia, a congregation hall for Shiites to mourn the death of Husayn ibn Ali in the month of Muharram; a husayni…
parole.testo: From Urdu اِمام باڑا (imām bāṛā) or اِمام باڑَہ (imām bāṛa).

parole.significato: Psyllium (Plantago ovata syn. Plantago ispaghula and Plantago afra syn. Plantago psyllium).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu اسپغول (ispaġol), from Classical Persian اسپغول (ispaġōl), from اسپ (asp, “horse”) + غول (ġōl, “ear”), because of the shape of its seeds.

parole.significato: a rally.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu جَلْسَہ (jalsa, “gathering”).

parole.significato: A cashmere shawl with coloured patterns.
parole.testo: From Urdu جامہ وار.

parole.significato: A former rank in the British Indian Army, the lowest rank for a viceroy's commissioned officer.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu جمعدار (jamadār), from Persian جمعدار (jam'-dār), from Arabic جَمْع (jamʕ, “gathering”) + Persian ـدار (-dār, “bearer”).

parole.significato: A ROSCA in Pakistan (an informal rotating pool-in monthly money saving scheme).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu کَمیٹی (kameṭī), itself from committee.

parole.significato: Finely chopped mince as used in South Asia cookery, typically lamb with peas or potatoes and spices, sometimes used as…
parole.testo: From Urdu قیمہ, from Persian قیمه (qime), from Turkic, perhaps Ottoman Turkish قیمه (kıyma), whence Turkish kıyma. Doublet of gheimeh, an Iranian meat stew.

parole.significato: A house-steward or native servant, being in charge of the kitchen and the food supplies.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu خانسامان, from خان (xān, “master”) + سامان (sāmān, “household goods”).

parole.significato: Of crops: cultivated and harvested during the monsoon season.
parole.testo: From Urdu خریف (xarīf), from Arabic خَرِيف (ḵarīf, “autumn”)

parole.significato: The arse.
parole.testo: Calque of Urdu درہ خیبر (dara xaibar).

parole.significato: The governor of a fort or large town in medieval India.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu قلعہ دار (qilādār).

parole.significato: A political environment in which politicians have a tendency to switch loyalties frequently for personal gain.
parole.testo: From Urdu لوٹاکریسی, from لوٹا (loṭā, “lota”), + -cracy; the lota is a water pot with a shape such that it falls over very easily. The term was coined in Pakistan in the early 1990s.

parole.significato: The last couplet of a ghazal, typically incorporating the poet's pen name in a creative way.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu مقطع, from Persian.

parole.significato: A percussion instrument thought to have originated in Africa
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu مرفع (marfa’), ultimately from Yemeni Arabic مرفع (marfa’, “kettledrum”).

parole.significato: A large wild goat, Capra falconeri, especially Capra falconeri megaceros, syn. Capra megaceros, having huge flattened s…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu مارخور (mārxor), from Classical Persian مَارْخْوَر (mārxwar, literally “snake-eater”), from مَار (mār, “snake”) + خْوَر (xwar) (present stem of خْوَرْدَن (xwardan, “to eat”)).

parole.significato: An imam; a Muslim doctor of law.
parole.testo: From Urdu مولوی (maulvi), and its source, Classical Persian مولوی (mawlawī), noun use of Arabic مَوْلَوِيّ (mawlawiyy, “of a lord or master”), ultimately from مَوْلًى (mawlan, “master”). Compare Mevlevi, mullah, maulana.

parole.significato: In parts of South Asia, a gathering where poetry or classical music is performed for a small audience in an intimate se…
parole.testo: From Urdu محفل (mahfil), from Arabic مَحْفِل (maḥfil, “festive gathering to entertain or praise someone”).

parole.significato: A Hindu religious festival.
parole.testo: From Urdu میلہ (mela)/Hindi मेला (melā), from Sanskrit मेलक (melaka).

parole.significato: A type of enamelwork Persian jewellery, especially champlevé.
parole.testo: From Urdu میناکاری (menākārī), from Persian [Term?].

parole.significato: Jasmine (the flower).
parole.testo: Urdu

parole.significato: A village or revenue estate.
parole.testo: From Urdu موضع (mauze', mauza'). Doublet of mouza.

parole.significato: A clerk or secretary.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu منشی (munšī, “secretary; munshi”) or directly from its etymon Classical Persian منشی (munšī, “secretary; munshi”), from Arabic مُنْشِئ (munšiʔ, “teacher; writer”).

parole.significato: A shout of hatred; "death to".
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu مردہ باد (murda bād, “death to”), from Persian مرده باد (morde bâd).

parole.significato: A poetic symposium in North India and Pakistan at which poets gather to perform their works, traditionally ghazals.
parole.testo: From Urdu مشاعره (mušā’ira).

parole.significato: an inflated skin-bag for water, variously said to be made from goats, from cows or from dogs, often by bheesties.
parole.testo: From Urdu مشک (maśak) / Hindi मशक (maśak), from Persian مشک (mašk), from Middle Persian [script needed] (mšk' /⁠mašk⁠/), from Old Persian 𐎶𐏁𐎣𐎠 (m-š-k-a /⁠maškā⁠/), via Aramaic or another descendant of Proto-Semitic *mašk- (“skin”).

parole.significato: A native accountant in the British Raj.
parole.testo: From Urdu متصدی (mutaṣaddī, “accountant, clerk”)

parole.significato: A deputy.
parole.testo: From Urdu نائب (nāib) / Hindi नाइब (nāib), नायब (nāyab), from Arabic نَائِب (nāʔib).

parole.significato: a person regular in salah; one who goes to the mosque (Islamic equivalent of a parishioner)
parole.testo: From Urdu نَمازی (namāzī), from Urdu نَماز (namāz) and their source, Persian نَمَاز.

parole.significato: The chief elected official of a local government in Pakistan.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu ناظم, ultimately from Arabic ناظم.

parole.significato: The hereditary sovereign of Hyderabad, a former state of India.
parole.testo: From Urdu نظام (nizām) and its source, Persian نظام (nezâm), short for نظام الملک (nezâm el-malek, “a ruler of the realm”).

parole.significato: An Indian rug or mat made with chain stitch.
parole.testo: From Urdu نمدا (namdā), from Persian [script needed] (namad, “carpet”), probably related to Sanskrit नमत (namata, “something woolen”), नवत (navata, “woolen cloth”).

parole.significato: Something whose name is unknown or unimportant; a thingy; a whatsit.
parole.testo: Unknown. Perhaps formed in English from a similar term; compare whosit, whaddayacallit. Perhaps coined as an exotic-sounding nonsense word. Perhaps from Persian or Urdu حجت (hujjat, “argument”), from Arabic حجة (ḥujja, “argument; pretext”). Attested from the early 20th century.

parole.significato: Something that one cannot name or does not know the name of; a whatsit.
parole.testo: Unknown. Perhaps from Urdu ḥujjat kāfī fīhi (“argument is sufficient”); compare oojah. Sornig (see quotations below) suggests derivation from Neapolitan agio capit (“I've understood”), but seems to be alone in this suggestion. Attested from the 1910s, often described as soldiers’ or sailors’ slang.

parole.significato: A villager; rustic; hick.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu [Term?].

parole.significato: Synonym of juz.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu پاره (pāra), from Persian پاره (pâre).

parole.significato: An administrative unit of British Raj, consisting of a number of villages. Since Indian independence, replaced by the b…
parole.testo: From Urdu پَرَگْنَہ (paragna) (Hindi परगना (paragnā)), from Persian پرگنة.

parole.significato: A mild curry made with cream, coconut milk, and almonds.
parole.testo: Urdu پسندہ, related to a word meaning "the favourite one", referring to a prime cut of meat.

parole.significato: An official who visits agricultural lands and maintains records of their ownership and tilling.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu پَٹْوَاری (paṭvārī) / Hindi पाटवारी (pāṭvārī) or Bengali পাটোয়ারি (paṭōẇari, “rent collector”).

parole.significato: A person of excellent character.
parole.testo: From Urdu پکا صاحِب / Hindi पक्का साहिब (pakkā sāhib, “genuine master”).

parole.significato: Belonging to the Ahmadiyya Muslim Jama'at movement.
parole.testo: From Urdu قادیانی (qādiyānī); which means "of Qadian" from Qadian, a town in Punjab, India; the location in which the religious movement began.

parole.significato: A style of Muslim devotional music, especially among the South Asian Sufis, accompanied by drums and harmonium.
parole.testo: From Urdu قوالی (qawwālī), from Classical Persian قوالی (qawwālī).

parole.significato: A fort or fortress.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu قِلْعَہ (qil'a), borrowed from Classical Persian قَلْعَه /قِلْعَه (qal'a).

parole.significato: The sacrifice of a livestock animal during Eid al-Adha.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu قُرْبَانی (qurbānī), from Classical Persian قُرْبَانِی (qurbānī), ultimately from Arabic قُرْبَان (qurbān).

parole.significato: A peasant or agricultural labourer in South Asia.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu رَعِیَّت (ra'iyat, “peasant”), from Classical Persian رعیت (ra'iyyat, “peasants; population”), from Arabic رَعِيَّة (raʕiyya, “flock, herd”).

parole.significato: The rigorous practice of Hindustani classical music.
parole.testo: From Urdu ریاض f (riyāz).

parole.significato: Plain, without spices or stuffing.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu سادہ (sāda).

parole.significato: Any of a breed of short-horned dairy cattle originating from the Sahiwal district.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu ساہِیوَال (sāhīvāl).

parole.significato: A slogan calling for the killing of blasphemers against Islam.
parole.testo: From Urdu سر تن سے جدا (sar tan seh judā, “separate the head from the body; beheading”), سر (“head”) + تن (“body”) + سے (se, “from”) + جدا (“separate”). Shortening of Urdu گستاخ رسول کی ایک ہی سزا سر تن سے جدا (Gustākh-e-Rasūl kī ek hī sazā, sar tan sē judā, “there is only one punishment for insulti

parole.significato: A kind of drinks stall or roadside pushcart selling teh tarik, historically and traditionally run by immigrants from Pa…
parole.testo: From Urdu شربت (śarbat, “sharbat; a type of sweet drink”), from Classical Persian شربت (šarbat).

parole.significato: Governmental.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu سَرْکاری (sarkārī) / Hindi सरकारी (sarkārī).

parole.significato: An ornament placed in front of the turban, worn by significant Hindu, Sikh and Muslim princes.
parole.testo: From Urdu سرپیچ/Hindi सरपेच (sarpec), from Persian سرپیچ (sarpeč, “socket”).

parole.significato: A pair of loose trousers worn (typically with a kameez and dupatta) by women in South Asia.
parole.testo: From Urdu شرارہ.

parole.significato: A knee-length coat that buttons to the neck, worn by men in parts of India and Pakistan.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu شیروانی (śervānī)/Hindi शेरवानी (śervānī), from the name of a town in Persia.

parole.significato: To hunt; to go hunting.
parole.testo: From Urdu شکار / Hindi शिकार (śikār), from Classical Persian شکار (šikār).

parole.significato: A hunter or tracker, especially in the Indian subcontinent.
parole.testo: From Urdu شکاری / Hindi शिकारी (śikārī), from Classical Persian شکاری (šikārī, “of hunting”), from شکار (šikār, “hunting, game”).

parole.significato: A high-ranking person in India and other areas of west-central Asia; a chief, a headman.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu سردار, Hindi सरदार (sardār), from Persian سردار (sardâr). Doublet of serdar and Sardar.

parole.significato: The Qur'an.
parole.testo: From sky + book. Also Calque of Urdu آسمانی کتاب (asmānī kitāb, “heavenly book”), a popular term used in Pakistan for the Quran. Referring to the belief that the Quran was first revealed by an angel to Muhammad, a prophet in Islam, so it is considered as a book from Heaven.

parole.significato: A mounted procession; a cavalcade.
parole.testo: From Urdu سوار (savār, “swordsman”), borrowed from Persian سوار (savâr, “rider”), from Old Persian 𐎠𐎿𐎲𐎠𐎼 (a-s-b-a-r /⁠asabāra-⁠/, “horseman”), from Proto-Iranian *Hacwabāráh, ultimately from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Haćwabʰāras.

parole.significato: A province of the Mughal Empire.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu صوبہ (sūbā, “province”).

parole.significato: A tribe in northern Pakistan cis-Indus region of Hazara, originally migrating from the Swat their ancestral homeland.
parole.testo: From Urdu سواتی (svātī).

parole.significato: An invoice or schedule.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu تعلیقہ (ta'līqa), from Arabic تَعْلِيقَة (taʕlīqa).

parole.significato: A hereditary estate in parts of India; subsequently, an administrative subdivision of a district.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu تَعَلُّق (ta'alluq), borrowed from Classical Persian تَعَلُّق (ta'alluq), borrowed from Arabic تَعَلُّق (taʕalluq), from تَعَلَّقَ (taʕallaqa).

parole.significato: Synonym of dak (“post system by means of relays of horses carrying mail and passengers”).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu ٹَپّال (ṭappāl) (Deccani), from Telugu టపాలు (ṭapālu).

parole.significato: A complimentary present; an honorarium.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu تَشْرِیف (taśrīf).

parole.significato: An administrative officer in Pakistan and India who gathers taxes from a tehsil.
parole.testo: From Urdu تحصیل دار (taḥṣīl dār), from Persian تحصیلدار, from Arabic تَحْصِيل (taḥṣīl), and Persian دار (dâr).

parole.significato: The commander of a thana; a police chief.
parole.testo: From Urdu ثاندار (thānadār), from ثانا (thānā, “thana”) + دار- (-dār, “holder”).

parole.significato: An underground chamber in which to keep cool during the heat of the day.
parole.testo: From Urdu تہ خانہ (teh xānā).

parole.significato: a master, especially of music, in South Asia and the Middle East
parole.testo: From Urdu استاد (ustād), from Classical Persian استاد (ustād, “master”).

parole.significato: An attorney, lawyer or agent.
parole.testo: From Urdu وکیل (vakīl) or Hindi वकील (vakīl), from Arabic وَكِيل (wakīl, “agent”).

parole.significato: A form of bride exchange in Pakistan and Afghanistan, involving the simultaneous marriage of a pair (brother and sister…
parole.testo: Urdu وٹہ سٹہ, literally "give-take".

parole.significato: tyranny, oppression
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu یزیدیت (yazīdiyat), Named after Yazid ibn Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan, the second ruler of the Umayyad Caliphate who is considered the killer of Imam al-Husayn at Karbala'.

parole.significato: An Indian landowner who collected local taxes and paid them to the British government.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu زمیندار (zamīndār, “landlord”), from Persian زمیندار.

parole.significato: A kind of embroidery using gold or silver thread.
parole.testo: From Urdu زردوزی (zardōzī, “gold embroidery”), from Classical Persian زردوزی (zardōzī, “gold embroidery”). See there for more.

parole.significato: An Islamic shrine
parole.testo: From Urdu زیارت.
